content.text:
Elon Musk is no longer a trillionaire after a global rout in tech shares wiped $500bn (£379bn) off his fortune.
The tech mogul became the first person ever to reach the milestone after the record-breaking listing of his rocket company SpaceX this month.
However, its shares have fallen around 30pc from their peak last week, while Tesla, Mr Musk's car company, was swept up in a widespread sell-off of technology stocks on Tuesday.
His wealth now stands at $957.1bn, according to analysis by Bloomberg. Calculations by Forbes suggested his net worth peaked at $1.45tn last week.
The decline in his personal fortune over the past week is worth more than the entire wealth of Larry Page, the world's second-richest man, whose fortune stands at just under $297bn.
Mr Musk's riches have been hit after stocks on Wall Street plunged for two consecutive days this week.
More than $89bn was wiped off the value of Tesla as its shares fell 5.8pc on Tuesday. The world's most valuable public company, Nvidia, declined by 4.1pc.
Mr Musk faces potential further pain as traders warned the sell-off could resume after Micron, a trillion-dollar artificial intelligence (AI) chips business, announces its third-quarter results later.
The chipmaker sank by 13.2pc on Tuesday as concerns grow that AI valuations have become overstretched.
Goldman Sachs cautioned this week that AI-linked stocks have become vulnerable to any signs of a slowdown in spending by tech giants.
Ben McKeown, investment manager at Dowgate Wealth, said Mr Musk was vulnerable to extreme swings in his wealth, as most of it is concentrated in just two companies: Tesla and SpaceX.
He said: "The old adage is, you concentrate to build wealth and diversify to keep it.
"Musk is the most extreme example of this. Almost his entire net worth sits in Tesla and SpaceX, which have been extremely volatile, especially SpaceX as the shareholder base starts to be unlocked and becomes free to sell."
Mr Musk became the world's first trillionaire on June 12 after the record-breaking listing of SpaceX.
Its shares surged by as much as 67pc in its opening three days in a frenzy of buying on Wall Street, after a record-breaking initial public offering that valued it at more than $1.8tn.
However, its stock then fell for three consecutive days, shedding around $928bn in market value from a peak of $2.9tn to just over $2tn. It rose 1pc on Tuesday despite the tech rout.
The decline in Mr Musk's wealth in the last week is the largest in history.
He previously held the record for the single-biggest loss in wealth of any individual when his fortune declined by an estimated $165bn in 2022 as shares in Tesla, his electric-car business, plunged.
